findings.title: Salesforce sync v2 broke integration setup: connect rate fell from 69% to 52% and questions spiked
findings.claim: In PostHog, integration setups that finished (integration_connected / integration_setup_started) were 547/789 = 69% in the weeks of 2026-04-06 to 2026-07-13. After the Salesforce sync v2 release on 2026-07-14, the rate fell to 256/497 = 52% (weeks of 2026-07-20 to 2026-09-21). AskRight salesforce_sync questions went from 0 before July to 40, peaking at 9 in the week of 2026-08-03 and 7 in the week of 2026-08-10. They cost 1,364 minutes, about 34 minutes per question. The only setup guide still says it 'applies to the original Salesforce sync connector'. This works against FY2026 goal 4: CRM sync set up in under 15 minutes.
findings.recommendation: Engineering (owner) should find where v2 setups drop off between setup_started and connected and fix it. Instrument time-to-connect to track the 15-minute goal. Rewrite the Salesforce sync setup guide for v2 within the next sprint. Hold any further connector changes until the connect rate is back to about 69%.

findings.title: Support questions are growing faster than active users, against the efficient-growth goal
findings.claim: AskRight questions averaged 16.75 per week in April (67 over the 4 weeks from 2026-04-06) and 30.8 per week in August (154 over the 5 weeks from 2026-08-03), up 84%. Weekly active users (users with task_completed) rose only about 42% over the same period, from about 2,109 to about 2,999. So questions per active user rose about 30%. Goal 3 requires questions per account to stay flat or fall. By total handling time, the largest topics are csv_import (2,973 min), custom_fields (1,835), salesforce_sync (1,364), workflow_editor (1,233) and billing_invoices (961).
findings.recommendation: Track questions per active account-month on the goals dashboard. Assign each owning team a reduction target for its topic: Engineering for csv_import and salesforce_sync, Product for custom_fields and workflow_editor, Finance & Ops for billing_invoices. Review progress monthly.

findings.title: The new-workflow-editor rollout more than doubled workflow editor questions
findings.claim: workflow_editor questions averaged 2.0 per week before the flag (40 over the 20 weeks to 2026-08-10). After the 50% rollout on 2026-08-18 and the 100% rollout on 2026-08-25, they averaged 4.4 per week (31 over 7 weeks), peaking at 8 in the week of 2026-08-31. The workflow_saved/workflow_editor_opened ratio stayed at about 0.49–0.50, so the new editor gives no visible usage gain to offset the extra support load. The top answerer handles 49% of these questions.
findings.recommendation: Product should review the questions asked since 2026-08-18 and add in-app guidance or fixes for the top confusions. Evaluate future flags on support load as well as usage, and use a holdout group instead of jumping from 50% to 100% within a week.

findings.title: CSV import is the most expensive support topic, and questions doubled around CSV import v2
findings.claim: csv_import had 83 questions and 2,973 minutes of handling time, the most of any topic, at about 36 minutes per question. Before 2026-05-25 it averaged 1.75 questions per week (14 in 8 weeks). From the week of 2026-06-01 (CSV import v2 was released 2026-06-02) it averaged 3.5 per week (63 in 18 weeks). Import completion (csv_import_completed/started) dipped from about 75–79% to 68–72% in the weeks right after the release, then recovered to about 75–80%.
findings.recommendation: Engineering should identify the most common import errors behind these questions. Add validation messages and a downloadable template inside the importer. Publish a CSV import v2 help article so Customer Success stops spending about 36 minutes per question.

findings.title: Salesforce sync knowledge sits mostly with one person
findings.claim: One answerer handles 77% of salesforce_sync questions (top_answerer_share 0.77; 40 questions and 1,364 minutes). That is far higher than any other meaningful topic: checklist_builder is next at 0.50, then workflow_editor at 0.49. Salesforce is one of the two core CRMs for Fernwell's target customers.
findings.recommendation: Have that answerer write a runbook for v2 troubleshooting. Pair them with at least two Engineering and Customer Success teammates on the next salesforce_sync questions until the top share falls below 50%. Apply the same approach to checklist_builder and workflow_editor.

findings.title: Billing and pricing confusion is a large question load, and average revenue per customer is below list price on every plan
findings.claim:
billing_invoices is the most frequent topic, with 88 questions (961 min), and pricing_plans adds 47 (478 min): 135 combined. billing_invoices hit 7 in a week on 2026-07-27, 2026-08-03 and 2026-09-21. Average Stripe MRR per customer is below list on every plan, even though extra seats should push it above:
- Starter: $76.45 vs $79
- Growth: $335.53 vs $349
- Scale: $955.78 vs $990
Enterprise averages $2,069 per month and is custom priced.
findings.recommendation: Finance & Ops and Sales should reconcile Stripe prices against the pricing page. Find out how much of the gap comes from annual discounts and how much from off-list deals. Fix the pricing page so annual pricing and seat overages are explicit. Publish a billing FAQ to cut billing_invoices questions.

findings.title: Custom fields take long to answer and questions are rising
findings.claim: custom_fields had 72 questions and 1,835 minutes of handling time, about 25 minutes each and the second-largest total. Weekly counts rose from 1–3 in April to 5–7 in some weeks: 6 on 2026-07-13, 5 on 2026-07-20, 5 on 2026-08-17 and 7 on 2026-09-07. No release explains the rise.
findings.recommendation: Product should group the custom_fields questions by theme. Ship in-product help or default field templates for the top two themes.

findings.title: Signups dipped in August after campaigns ended, and some campaigns barely produce signups
findings.claim: HubSpot campaign signups were 103 in July, 66 in August and 107 in September. PostHog weekly signed_up fell from about 50–65 in May–June to 34–39 in most August weeks. Q2 Paid Search ended in June (62 signups) and Partner Webinar Series ended in August (91 signups). Founder Podcast Tour produced only 5 signups and Summer Launch Week only 9. Meanwhile LinkedIn: Onboarding Playbook grew from 13 to 38 per month, and Q3 Retargeting reached 36 in September.
findings.recommendation: Plan replacement campaigns before current ones end so signups don't gap. Move budget away from Founder Podcast Tour-style one-offs toward LinkedIn: Onboarding Playbook and Q3 Retargeting. Check that these campaigns' signups activate and retain before scaling them further.

findings.title: The activation goal cannot be tracked with current reports
findings.claim: The top FY2026 goal is 65% activation (checklist_launched within 14 days of signup). PostHog reports only aggregate weekly events: 32–65 signed_up per week against 386–923 checklist_launched users, mostly from existing accounts. That cannot measure activation by signup cohort or by acquisition source. Retention by source (goal 2) is not reported either.
findings.recommendation: Build an account-level cohort report that joins PostHog signed_up and checklist_launched within 14 days with the HubSpot campaign and Stripe MRR. This lets activation and day-90 retention be tracked by acquisition source.

findings.title: "Pricing and packaging" disagrees with Stripe on the Growth plan
findings.statement: The "Pricing and packaging" doc (owner: Head of Sales) disagrees with Stripe on the Growth plan: seats included: doc says 10, Stripe has 5; annual discount: doc says 20%, Stripe has 15%. The plan carries $134.2K MRR, so quotes from the doc won't match invoices.
findings.label: fact

recommendation.action: Decide which Growth terms are right (seats included: doc says 10, Stripe has 5; annual discount: doc says 20%, Stripe has 15%). If Stripe is, correct "Pricing and packaging" (Head of Sales); if the doc is, change the Growth price in Stripe. Until then, quote Growth from Stripe.

findings.narrative: Quotes for the Growth plan won't match invoices, because the "Pricing and packaging" doc disagrees with Stripe. The doc says 10 seats included and a 20% annual discount, while Stripe has 5 seats and 15%. The plan carries $134.2K MRR, so decide which terms are right and fix the doc or Stripe to match, and quote Growth from Stripe until then.
